hints.title: Root-to-Leaf Remainder Obstacle
hints.text: Paths must start at the root and terminate strictly at a leaf node. How can you recursively subtract each node's value from the remaining target until a leaf with a matching remainder is reached?

hints.title: Target Reduction Invariant
hints.text: At any node, a valid root-to-leaf path exists if subtracting the current value leaves zero at a leaf, or if a valid path exists in either subtree with the reduced target.

hints.title: Leaf Validation Procedure
hints.text: If root is null, return false. If root is a leaf (neither left nor right child), return targetSum == root.val. Otherwise, recursively check hasPathSum on left and right children with targetSum - root.val, returning their logical OR.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of nodes in tree (0 <= N <= 5000)
complexity.notes: Single recursive depth-first pass checking all root-to-leaf paths.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Failing to check that a node is strictly a leaf can falsely accept paths terminating at internal nodes.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Strict leaf verification: not root.left and not root.right.
